question.prompt: The function \(f\) is defined by \[f(x) = \lfloor|x|\rfloor - |\lfloor x \rfloor|\] for all real numbers \(x,\) where \(\lfloor r \rfloor\) denotes the greatest integer less than or equal to the real number \(r.\) What is the range of \(f?\)

solutions.title: Separate inputs by sign and integrality
solutions.explanation:
For nonnegative inputs, absolute value changes nothing. Negative inputs require separating integers from nonintegers because the floor function rounds downward.

If \(x\geq0\), then \(|x|=x\) and \(\lfloor x\rfloor\geq0\), so
\[
f(x)=\lfloor x\rfloor-\lfloor x\rfloor=0.
\]
If \(x<0\) is an integer, both \(\lfloor|x|\rfloor\) and \(|\lfloor x\rfloor|\) equal \(-x\), again giving \(f(x)=0\).

If \(x<0\) is not an integer, write \(x=-k-t\), where \(k\) is a nonnegative integer and \(0<t<1\). Then
\[
\lfloor|x|\rfloor=\lfloor k+t\rfloor=k,
\qquad \lfloor x\rfloor=-k-1.
\]
Consequently,
\[
f(x)=k-|-k-1|=k-(k+1)=-1.
\]
These cases cover every real input. Both outputs occur, since \(f(0)=0\) and \(f(-\tfrac12)=-1\). The range is therefore \(\boxed{\{-1,0\}}\), choice \(\text{A}\).
